Topics · Is there a God?

Why trust anything I haven't seen for myself?

Your name, your birthday, the earth's shape: you were told. So the real question is how to weigh a report.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُم مِّنۢ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِكُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْـًٔا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَـٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ ۙ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And Allāh has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing, and He made for you hearing and vision and hearts [i.e., intellect] that perhaps you would be grateful.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:78

Translation

The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Yahweh has made even both of them.

Original · Hebrew

אֹ֣זֶן שֹׁ֭מַעַת וְעַ֣יִן רֹאָ֑ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה גַם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

Proverbs · 20:12

World English Bible

Try a short list. Your date of birth. Who your parents are. That a country you have never visited exists. That your medicine does what the label says. You checked almost none of it. You were told, and you were right to believe it. So trusting a report is no lapse from reason. It is how most knowing works. This verse begins there: you came into the world knowing nothing, and hearing is the first thing named among what you were given.

A question for you

Name one thing you are sure of and have never checked yourself.

Part 2 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟ أَن تُصِيبُوا۟ قَوْمًۢا بِجَهَـٰلَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَـٰدِمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:6

Translation

Question your neighbor; it may be he didn’t say it. If he has said it, it may be that he may not say it again. Question a friend; for many times there is slander. Don’t trust every word.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἔλεγξον τὸν φίλον, μήποτε οὐκ εἶπε, καὶ εἰ εἴρηκεν, ἵνα μὴ δευτερώσῃ. Ἔλεγξον φίλον, πολλάκις γὰρ γίνεται διαβολὴ, καὶ μὴ παντὶ λόγῳ πίστευε.

Sirach · 19:14-15

World English Bible

﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ ۚ فَسْـَٔلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message]. So ask the people of the message [i.e., former scriptures] if you do not know.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:43

So trust is not the problem. The problem is knowing when to stop. Four questions do most of the work. Was the speaker in a position to know? Do they seem honest? Do several witnesses agree who could not have coordinated? Is there any reason for doubt: a motive, a contradiction, a record of errors? This verse gives the rule in a line: when someone unreliable brings news, check it before you act. It says verify. It does not say refuse.

A question for you

Which question do you lean on most when you hear something important?

If you sayWho is telling me?
ThenThen character and position are your measures. People are poor at spotting lies, which is why one witness is rarely enough.
If you sayDo others, independently, say the same?
ThenThat is the strongest of them. Many independent reports can come close to certainty, though independence is harder to show than it looks, especially inside one community.
If you sayWhat do they gain by it?
ThenA good check, and one that can be put to anyone, including this app, which sells nothing and asks for nothing.

Part 3 of 3

﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَـٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer,[9] and spend out of what We[10] have provided for them,

Translator's notes

[9] At its proper times and according to its specified conditions. [10] It is to be noted that the reference of Allāh (Subḥānahu wa taʿālā) to Himself as "We" in many Qur’ānic verses is necessarily understood in the Arabic language to denote grandeur and power, as opposed to the more intimate singular form "I" used in specific instances.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:3

Give to the Most High according as he has given. As your hand has found, give generously. For the Lord repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.

Sirach · 35:10-11

World English Bible

One reply is fair: a report about the past is one thing, a report about the unseen quite another. Yet you reason to the unseen every day. You cannot see another person's mind. You infer it from words and acts. No one watched the early universe. It is reasoned to from traces. This verse names trust in the unseen first among the qualities it praises. Whether that road reaches God is the open question. Being unseen is not enough to rule it out.

A question for you

What seems the biggest difference between trusting a report of a country and a report of God?

If you sayAnyone can go and check the country.
ThenThat is the real difference. A claim about God needs another kind of check, and that is what the next questions look for.
If you sayGod's existence is a far bigger claim.
ThenBigger claims need more weighing, and that is fair. The question is how much.
If you sayThe people who report God disagree.
ThenThey do, on much, and they agree on more than people expect. Disagreement is a reason for care, not for giving up the question.

The same in the other books
